Dialtune is a cable tuning system for drums. Using separate dials for the top and bottom heads, drummers can find the exact sound they're looking for faster, change drumheads in under a minute, and explore new creative possibilities without compromise. While Cable tuning is not new, Dialtune has improved upon it with a patented system that makes it the only cable-tuning drum that can independently tune the top and bottom heads using separate dials on either side of the drum. Additionally, changing drumheads doesn't require removing the cable. Dialtune's quick-release hoops make changing a drumhead simple and easy.

I recently went through a breakup, and it has hit me hard. I thought we had a future together, and now I feel lost and alone. This event triggered my depression even more, and I'm struggling to cope with the pain.

Breakups can be incredibly difficult and it's understandable that you're feeling lost and alone right now. It sounds like this breakup has had a significant impact on your mental health, particularly triggering your depression. Coping with the pain can feel overwhelming, but there are steps you can take to help yourself through this challenging time.

Firstly, it may be helpful to give yourself permission to grieve the loss of the relationship. Breakups involve a sense of loss, and allowing yourself to acknowledge and process those feelings is an important part of healing. Give yourself space and time to experience the emotions that come up, whether it's sadness, anger, or confusion.

It could also be beneficial to reach out for support from friends, family, or even a therapist. Talking about your feelings with someone who cares about you can provide comfort and perspective. Additionally, a therapist can offer guidance and tools to help you navigate through this difficult period. They can assist you in developing coping strategies specific to your situation and provide a safe space for you to express your emotions without judgment.

Engaging in self-care activities can also play a crucial role in managing your depression during this time. Focus on activities that bring you joy and help you relax, such as exercise, spending time in nature, practicing mindfulness or meditation, pursuing hobbies, or engaging in creative outlets. Taking care of your physical health by maintaining a balanced diet, getting enough sleep, and avoiding excessive alcohol or drug use can also contribute to your overall well-being.

Lastly, try to challenge any negative thoughts or beliefs that may be fueling your depression. Remind yourself that breakups are a common part of life and do not define your worth as a person. Surround yourself with positive affirmations and engage in activities that boost your self-esteem and confidence.

Remember, healing takes time, and it's okay to have ups and downs along the way. Be patient and kind to yourself as you navigate through this challenging period.

I had to put a restraining order against my ex-fiancé. He was served last night. He was mentally and verbally abusive towards me. I thought it was my nerves, but every time I stand up, I get sick. If I sit and rock, I'm fine.

Hello, and thank you for your question. You may be right, your physical symptoms of getting sick to your stomach may very well be your nerves or anxiety. That is totally normal and understandable given your circumstances. Another thing that is not unusual is that you feel better when you sit and rock. That is actually a fairly common way that many people comfort themselves in times of high stress. If you are concerned that there is an actual physical illness causing these symptoms, you may want to visit your primary care provider. They may tell you that they don't see anything physically wrong with you, and at that point you may want to visit a counselor about the symptoms and your relationship experience. A visit with a counselor may be a good idea either way. I work as a counselor in primary care, and I promise you that many people have very real physical symptoms when they have gone through abuse. Unexplainable stomach and headaches are very common. Sometimes, with counseling, those physical symptoms actually stop. Be well, and I hope you feel better soon.Robin J. Landwehr, DBH, LPCC, NCC

Building and maintaining healthy relationships can be challenging, especially when you have a fear of abandonment. It takes courage to acknowledge this struggle, so I commend you for reaching out.

To begin addressing your fear of abandonment and building trust with others, it may be helpful to explore the root causes of these feelings. Reflecting on past experiences or traumas that may have contributed to your fear can provide valuable insights. Consider journaling about these experiences or discussing them with someone you trust.

In addition, practicing self-compassion is crucial in overcoming these challenges. Remind yourself that everyone has their own insecurities and fears, and it's okay to feel vulnerable. Take time to nurture your emotional well-being by engaging in activities that bring you joy and relaxation. This could include hobbies, exercise, spending time in nature, or connecting with supportive friends or family members.

Developing effective communication skills can also contribute to healthier relationships. Learning how to express your needs, boundaries, and concerns openly and assertively can help build trust and understanding with others. Additionally, active listening and empathy are important components of effective communication. Strive to genuinely listen to others' perspectives and validate their emotions.

Consider seeking support from a therapist or counselor who specializes in relationship issues if you haven't already done so. They can provide guidance tailored to your specific situation and offer tools to navigate your fear of abandonment. Remember, therapy is a safe space where you can explore your thoughts and emotions without judgment.

Lastly, remember that forming and maintaining healthy relationships is a journey that takes time and effort. Be patient with yourself as you work through these challenges, and celebrate small victories along the way. You deserve fulfilling connections, and with dedication and self-reflection, you can overcome your fear of abandonment and cultivate healthier relationships.

I've been feeling lost and uncertain about my career path. I've always had this pressure to choose a stable job that pays well, but deep down, I'm passionate about something completely different. I fear disappointing my family if I pursue my true passion instead of following their expectations. How do I navigate this conflict between societal expectations and my own desires? I can understand how challenging it must be to feel torn between societal expectations and your own passions when it comes to choosing a career path. It's not uncommon to experience this conflict, and it's important to remember that you're not alone in feeling this way.

Firstly, it might be helpful to take some time for self-reflection and exploration. Consider what truly brings you joy and fulfillment in life. What are the activities or subjects that make you lose track of time? Identifying your true passion can provide clarity and help guide your decision-making process.

Once you have a better understanding of your passion, it could be beneficial to research different career options related to that field. Look into various industries, job roles, and potential paths that align with your interests. This will allow you to gain insight into the possibilities available to you.

While it's natural to worry about disappointing your family, it's essential to prioritize your own happiness and well-being. Remember that pursuing your passion doesn't necessarily mean sacrificing stability or financial security. There may be ways to merge your passion with practicality by exploring alternative career routes, such as freelancing, starting your own business, or finding organizations that value your unique skills and interests.

It can also be helpful to seek support from individuals who have navigated similar situations or who understand the importance of following one's passion. Connect with like-minded communities, attend networking events, or even consider finding a mentor who can offer guidance and advice based on their own experiences.

Ultimately, finding fulfillment in a career that aligns with your passions is possible, but it may require patience, perseverance, and open-mindedness. Trust yourself and your abilities, and remember that your journey towards a fulfilling career is unique to you.

I really want to make some positive changes in my life, especially when it comes to my behavior. Lately, I've noticed that I have a tendency to lash out at people when I'm feeling stressed or overwhelmed. It's not fair to them, and it's not healthy for me either. I want to learn better coping mechanisms and find healthier ways to express my emotions.

It's great to hear that you're motivated to make positive changes in your life, especially when it comes to your behavior. Recognizing the tendency to lash out at people when feeling stressed or overwhelmed is a big step towards personal growth and healthier relationships.

To start, I would suggest exploring some coping mechanisms that can help you manage stress and express your emotions in a healthier way. One effective technique is deep breathing exercises. When you feel yourself getting overwhelmed, take a moment to focus on your breath. Inhale deeply through your nose, hold for a few seconds, and then exhale slowly through your mouth. This simple practice can help calm your mind and body during stressful situations.

Another helpful strategy is finding an outlet for your emotions. Engaging in activities like journaling, painting, playing music, or exercising can provide a healthy release for pent-up feelings. Find something that resonates with you and allows you to express yourself freely.

Additionally, practicing self-care is crucial for overall well-being. Make sure to prioritize activities that bring you joy and relaxation. It could be as simple as taking a walk in nature, listening to your favorite music, or spending quality time with loved ones. Taking care of yourself physically, emotionally, and mentally will contribute to a more balanced and resilient mindset.

Remember, change takes time and effort, so be patient with yourself throughout this process. Celebrate small victories along the way and don't hesitate to reach out for support from friends, family, or even online communities who may have similar experiences. You're not alone in this journey, and together we can find healthier ways to cope and express our emotions.

Depression looms over me, affecting every aspect of my life. Throughout this counseling session, my goal is to understand the underlying causes behind my depression and develop skills to overcome its grip on my emotions.
My emotional state oscillates between extreme sadness, constant exhaustion, and a lack of motivation. Simple tasks feel impossible, and even finding joy in activities I once loved seems out of reach. To cope with my depression, I've tried engaging in artistic outlets, reaching out to friends, and establishing structured routines. However, it's been challenging to maintain consistency and find lasting relief from these efforts.
I'm interested in exploring different therapeutic approaches used for treating depression and understanding how they could help me regain a sense of purpose and motivation. Additionally, I would appreciate insight into the potential benefits of medication as part of my treatment plan.

It sounds like you're going through a really tough time with depression, and I want to offer some guidance on how to address your concerns. First of all, I want to acknowledge the impact that depression is having on every aspect of your life. It's important to remember that seeking support and working towards understanding the underlying causes can be a significant step in overcoming its grip on your emotions.

The emotional rollercoaster you described, including extreme sadness, constant exhaustion, and lack of motivation, is so challenging to deal with. Simple tasks feeling impossible and losing joy in activities you once loved are common symptoms of depression. Changes in appetite and insomnia can further contribute to the overall impact on your daily functioning.

It's understandable that the end of a long-term relationship has triggered this depressive episode for you. The loss of companionship, support, and future plans can leave you feeling abandoned and hopeless. Heartbreak can be incredibly difficult to navigate, and it's completely normal for it to consume your thoughts and drain your energy.

You mentioned that you've tried engaging in artistic outlets, reaching out to friends, and establishing structured routines as coping mechanisms. These are great tools to incorporate into your self-care routine, and it's commendable that you've already taken steps to find relief. However, consistently maintaining these efforts and finding lasting relief can indeed be challenging. 

Exploring different therapeutic approaches for treating depression could potentially bring you the support and techniques you need to regain a sense of purpose and motivation. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is a commonly used approach that focuses on identifying negative thought patterns and developing healthier ways of thinking and behaving. You might also benefit from interpersonal therapy, which focuses on improving your relationships and communication skills. Another approach worth exploring is psychodynamic therapy, which delves into childhood experiences and their impact on your current struggles.

In terms of medication, it might be beneficial to consult with a mental health professional who can provide a comprehensive assessment and discuss the potential benefits and side effects of medication as part of your treatment plan. They will be able to evaluate if medication would be suitable for your specific situation.

Remember, this is just general guidance, and it's essential to seek professional help from someone who can provide personalized support based on their expertise. Keep in mind that there is hope for recovery, and taking these steps toward understanding and managing depression will bring you closer to regaining control over your emotions and finding a sense of purpose once again.

Fear is a part of life. In fact, our five main emotions are joy, fear, sadness, shame, and anger. In reality, you can do what is important to you while having your fears! My question for you is, what would you do if this fear was completely gone? It sounds like you're going through a challenging time with your anxiety symptoms, and I'm here to provide guidance and suggestions. It's important to remember that everyone's experiences with anxiety are unique, but there are some general strategies that may be helpful for you.

First, it could be beneficial to explore if any specific triggers or situations tend to bring on your anxiety symptoms. Keeping a journal of your thoughts, feelings, and the circumstances surrounding your anxiety episodes might help you identify patterns or common themes. This can offer valuable insight into potential underlying causes and allow you to develop personalized coping strategies.

To manage racing thoughts, it may be useful to practice mindfulness techniques. Mindfulness involves paying attention to the present moment without judgment. You can try deep breathing exercises or meditation to help redirect your focus from the worries in your mind to your breath or other sensations in your body.

For shortness of breath, practicing deep breathing exercises can also be helpful. Take slow, deliberate breaths in through your nose, filling up your abdomen, and exhale slowly through your mouth. This can activate the relaxation response in your body and alleviate some of the physical tension associated with anxiety.

Constant worries can be overwhelming, so implementing strategies to challenge and reframe negative thoughts may make a difference. Try questioning the validity of your worries or replacing them with more realistic or positive thoughts. For instance, if you find yourself constantly worrying about what others think of you, remind yourself that their opinions don't define your worth as a person.

In addition to these self-help strategies, consider reaching out to supportive friends, family members, or even joining a support group where you can connect with others who have similar experiences. Opening up to someone you trust about what you're going through can provide an additional source of comfort and understanding.

Although these strategies can be effective for many individuals, it's important to keep in mind that everyone's journey with anxiety is different. If your symptoms persist or significantly interfere with your daily life, seeking professional help from a mental health expert can be beneficial. They can offer personalized guidance and support tailored to your specific needs.

Remember, you have already taken an important step in acknowledging your anxiety and seeking strategies to cope with it. Be patient with yourself throughout this process as finding what works best for you may take time and experimentation. Keep focusing on self-care, practicing the suggested techniques, and reaching out to supportive individuals.

When you start counseling you don't yet know your counselor very well, so it's normal to keep your feelings in check until you feel comfortable and a bit more relaxed with your counselor and with the situation. Sometimes, though, there are emotions that have been waiting and waiting to finally find someone who will listen with a kind ear. If you feel safe right away in the situation with your counselor, you might just cry in spite of your fears about it. Your therapist is used to people expressing how they feel and will keep strict confidentiality, so even though it's embarrassing, finally experiencing someone truly listening with empathy and kindness may just be worth it. Hi! Thank you for your question. It's tough to be in a healthy and loving relationship when we believe we are not worth it. Quite often being in such a relationship is very uncomfortable as it goes against everything we believe about ourselves. First, I want to say you are very brave to open up yourself to the relationship with this wonderful woman you met. Second, I would like to invite you to treat yourself with compassion as you are entering this unknown territory for yourself. Doing something new and totally unfamiliar can be scary, so it's vital that you are kind and gentle with yourself. Acknowledge that what you are doing is scary and uncomfortable and that it will take some time to get used to it. Don't judge yourself and force yourself to feel a certain way. It's important that you are patient with yourself and tolerant of your discomfort. With time, space, kindness, and tolerance your discomfort and fear will start to dissolve. Invite your new partner to also relate to your feelings in the open and compassionate way. The worst thing that you or your partner can do is to rush your feelings, pressure you to feel in a different way or to say that there is something wrong with you cause you feel a certain way. My anxiety tends to intensify in situations where I am not in complete control. For example, traveling alone triggers extreme unease and apprehension as various unpredictable factors come into play. Fearful thoughts about potential accidents, mishaps, or getting lost constantly plague my mind, making it difficult to enjoy the experience fully.

An instance that demonstrated the extent of my anxiety occurred during a business trip last year. Although the opportunity for professional growth excited me, boarding the plane triggered intense worry and physical symptoms typical of anxiety. Nausea, sweating, and racing thoughts prevented me from sleeping properly during the flight and added another layer of distress to an already stressful trip.

The symptoms of my anxiety span from palpitations and dizziness to intrusive thoughts and restlessness. This constant state of worry frequently hinders my ability to focus or engage fully in everyday activities.

While I have attempted deep breathing exercises and exposure therapy, their impact has been rather limited when it comes to addressing the root causes of my anxiety. It's vital for me to explore a more comprehensive approach tailored specifically to managing travel-related anxiety and its associated triggers.

Are there specific interventions you would recommend for individuals dealing with travel-related anxiety? How can I reframe my thoughts to diminish the anticipatory anxiety I experience before embarking on a trip?

When it comes to managing travel-related anxiety, there are several interventions and strategies that may be helpful for you. Here are some suggestions:

1. Gradual exposure: Start by exposing yourself to situations that trigger anxiety in a gradual and controlled manner. For example, you can begin by taking short trips to nearby places before gradually increasing the distance. This allows you to build up your confidence and familiarity with traveling.

2. Planning and preparation: Engage in thorough planning and preparation before your trip. Researching your destination, creating a detailed itinerary, and having backup plans can help alleviate some of the uncertainties that contribute to anticipatory anxiety. Being well-prepared can also give you a sense of control over the situation.

3. Cognitive reframing: Pay attention to your thoughts and try to challenge negative or catastrophic thinking patterns. Instead of dwelling on worst-case scenarios, focus on realistic and positive possibilities. Remind yourself of successful past experiences or instances when everything went smoothly during your travels.

4. Self-care practices: Prioritize self-care activities such as regular exercise, adequate sleep, healthy eating, and relaxation techniques. Taking care of your physical well-being can have a positive impact on your mental health and overall resilience to stress and anxiety.

5. Mindfulness and grounding techniques: Practice mindfulness exercises and grounding techniques to help bring your focus back to the present moment and reduce racing thoughts. Deep breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, or engaging your senses through sensory objects can all be effective methods for managing anxiety symptoms.

6. Support network: Seek support from friends, family, or fellow travelers who understand your anxiety and can provide encouragement and reassurance. Sharing your concerns and fears with others can offer perspective and emotional support throughout your journey.

Remember, everyone's experience with anxiety is unique, so it might take some trial and error to find what works best for you. If these suggestions don't provide sufficient relief, consider reaching out to a mental health professional who can provide personalized guidance and support.

They achieve these impressive speeds through their slender build, flexible spine, and long legs, which allow them to take long strides and cover a lot of ground with each stride.

However, if we consider all animals, including those that fly or swim, the peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) is the fastest animal in the world. It can reach speeds of up to 240 miles per hour (386 kilometers per hour) during a hunting dive known as a stoop, making it the fastest animal in the world overall.

It's worth noting that different animals have different ways of measuring their speed, and some species are faster in certain situations than in others. However, in terms of pure top speed, the cheetah and peregrine falcon are among the fastest animals on the planet.

I have an amazing life, so why can't I just enjoy it?

It is not easy being a wife and mother. You have shifted roles in your life. You went from having a career to focusing on your family. Transitioning can be hard, especially when we feel we gave something up that we really wanted. I want to acknowledge you for wanting to be the best wife and mother you can. I think it is great that you are self-aware and want to work on this.Feeling "unhappy and trapped" may also mean that you are  believing these negative thoughts are absolutely true. We have lots and lots of thoughts throughout the day. Sometimes we pay a lot of attention to some and some we ignore. Right now these thoughts are getting a lot of your attention and perhaps you are thinking because you are thinking them they are true.  Is it really true that you trapped? You also said that you have an amazing life. It doesn't sound like you are only having negative thoughts. You have some positive ones, too. However, you are giving a lot of weight to the negative thoughts, more weight than the positive ones.I also wonder if you are struggling with the fact that you are even having this thought. One thing that can be helpful is to recognize that you are having a thought, that it is a negative thought, that thinking it does not make it true, and to let it go. This is the basis for mindfulness work that can be really helpful. It is a great place for you to start so you can balance out your thoughts and emotions.Best of luck to you!

The main issue is a lack of emotional connection between my partner and me. We used to have deep conversations and share our thoughts and feelings freely, but now it feels like we're disconnected. We spend most of our time together without really connecting on an emotional level. It's making me question whether my partner still cares about me or if they're losing interest. One specific situation that triggered these concerns was when I shared something important and vulnerable, but my partner seemed disinterested and distracted. It hurt me deeply because I expected their support and understanding. Can you guide me on how to deepen our emotional intimacy and discuss our needs openly?

Building and maintaining emotional connection in an intimate relationship is crucial for its growth and fulfillment. It's understandable that you're feeling disconnected and questioning your partner's level of interest and care. Let's work together to address these concerns and find ways to deepen the emotional intimacy between you and your partner.

1. Create a Safe Space: Start by creating a safe and non-judgmental space where both you and your partner can express yourselves openly. Be mindful of your tone and approach when communicating your feelings, ensuring that it encourages open dialogue rather than defensiveness or blame.

2. Practice Active Listening: Actively listen to each other during conversations without distractions. Put away electronic devices, make eye contact, and show genuine interest in what your partner has to say. This will help foster a sense of being heard and understood.

3. Set Aside Quality Time: Dedicate quality time to do activities together that facilitate emotional connection. Engage in shared hobbies or interests, go on dates, or participate in new experiences that allow for meaningful conversations and bonding opportunities.

4. Express Appreciation and Gratitude: Regularly acknowledge and express gratitude for the positive aspects of your relationship. Show appreciation for gestures, actions, or qualities you admire in your partner. This creates a positive atmosphere and reinforces the emotional connection between you.

5. Foster Emotional Vulnerability: Encourage vulnerability by sharing your own feelings and thoughts with your partner. When both individuals feel safe expressing their vulnerability, it fosters a deeper understanding and strengthens emotional bonds.

6. Explore Each Other's Love Languages: Discover and understand how you and your partner prefer to give and receive love. Take the free online quiz about love languages and discuss the results together. This knowledge helps you meet each other's emotional needs more effectively.

7. Seek Professional Help If Needed: If despite your efforts, you continue experiencing difficulties in deepening emotional intimacy, consider seeking professional assistance from a licensed couples therapist. They can provide personalized guidance and support tailored to your specific situation.

Remember, it takes time, effort, and open communication to rebuild emotional connection in a relationship. By implementing these suggestions and reflecting on each other's needs, you'll lay the foundation for a stronger and more satisfying emotional bond between you and your partner.

2. Review organizational policies: Familiarize yourself with your organization's policies regarding confidentiality and ethical conduct. This will give you a better understanding of the expectations and guidelines set by your workplace.

They may have experienced similar situations or can provide advice based on their own perspectives. Having a support system within your workplace can make it easier to navigate challenging situations.

I've been feeling extremely down lately and want assistance in overcoming my depression.
 To find ways to manage and alleviate symptoms of depression.

Recently, I've been lacking interest or pleasure in activities that I used to enjoy. It feels like a heavy weight is constantly pulling me down, and it's hard to muster up the motivation to do anything. My sleep patterns have been disrupted; some nights, I can't fall asleep at all, while others I oversleep and struggle to get out of bed in the morning. These feelings of sadness and hopelessness are really affecting my day-to-day life.

What steps can I take to improve my mood and regain a sense of normalcy?

It's difficult when you're feeling down and lacking interest in activities that used to bring you pleasure. The weight you feel pulling you down can make it challenging to find motivation. I understand how disrupted sleep patterns can add to your distress, making some nights restless while others lead to oversleeping.

To improve your mood and regain a sense of normalcy, here are a few suggestions:

1. Establish a Routine: Creating a daily routine can provide structure and stability. Try to wake up and go to bed at consistent times each day. Incorporate activities that you enjoy or used to enjoy, even if you don't currently feel motivated. Gradually engaging in pleasurable activities may help lift your mood over time.

2. Prioritize Self-Care: It's important to focus on self-care during this time. Ensure you're eating nutritious meals regularly, staying hydrated, and getting some exercise. Gentle physical activity like walking or stretching can have positive effects on your mental well-being. Practicing relaxation techniques such as deep breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, or mindfulness meditation might also help reduce stress.

3. Reach Out for Support: Consider speaking with trusted friends or family members about what you've been experiencing. Having someone lend an empathetic ear and offer support can prove invaluable. Additionally, there are various online communities or helplines where you can connect with individuals who are going through similar experiences. Sharing your feelings in these spaces can help alleviate some of the emotional burden.

4. Journaling: Writing down your thoughts, emotions, and experiences in a journal can be cathartic and help you gain insight into your feelings. You can reflect on any patterns or triggers that you notice, allowing for greater understanding and potential avenues for healing.

5. Engage in Relaxing Activities: Seek out activities that promote relaxation and joy. This could include listening to music, spending time in nature, reading a book, watching a favorite TV show or movie, or engaging in creative outlets like drawing, painting, or writing. I think it's a great idea that you are asking this question now while it's early on. The first thing I wonder is what age you are.  At different transitions and stages in life, it's really common for anxieties to come out of the woodwork.  First time this takes place at a greater level is during adolescence, because a teen's "job" is to figure out who they are within the context of other people.  Spikes in anxiety also can also occur after high school when you are leaving the nest and heading to college, or the late twenties when it feels like you are expected to have your life figured out and compare to where others are in their lives.  That same scenario can show up in mid-life as well for different reasons depending on the person.  Aside from age, certain circumstances can influence a jump in anxiety, such as a job change, switching schools, moving, opening a business, college finals, etc.  Take some time to explore where the anxiety might be coming from and just see what comes up.  It may be something you have some control over, or something that you can ask for help from someone else for--especially if it's social anxiety.  The more you practice social skills, the more confidence you'll have in the long-run.A metaphor I use with some people is gas for a car.  Anxiety is a necessary motivator for action, though you get to decide where to go with that anxiety.  An overfilled tank doesn't get you any further than a normally-filled tank, and more gas doesn't mean the gas is in charge of where you go.  Applying that to what I know about your situation--how much of that worrying is getting you somewhere, how much is just extra gas, and are the worries changing what you really want to do? Sometimes knowing the makeup of our anxiety gives us more power over how we deal with it, and I think you could for sure get there with some help.

 Trust is something that we earn based on our actions and the actions of people we interact with; it’s also based on our ability to communicate and understand what we value and have in common.  If you are focused on every little detail around your relationship, it may turn into an unhealthy obsession and it may harm your relationship more.   If instead you focus on opening the lines of communication, let him know what you expect from him, and discuss how you could both build trust again, you may become closer and give your relationship the opportunity to grow.  ¿Debería este molesta porque mi esposo me mintió de nuevo?Estoy tratando de hacer que mi matrimonio funcione después de una separación.  Antes de separarnos el mentía mucho y rompía todas sus promesas.  No creo que me haya sido infiel.  El mes pasado, le pregunté cuantas mujeres trabajan con él, y él me dijo.  Ayer, me enteré que se olvido de una muchacha.  ¿Debería estar enojada?¿Quieres estar molesta porque se le olvido con cuantas mujeres trabaja?  Piénsalo por un momento.  ¿Quieres determinar la confianza que le tienes en tu esposo basándote en su capacidad de reportar la cantidad de mujeres que trabajan con él?  Si tu respuesta es sí, ¿qué refleja eso sobre tu matrimonio?  La confianza es algo que se gana basado en nuestras acciones y las de aquellos con quienes interactuamos; también en nuestra habilidad de comunicar y entender los valores que tenemos en común. Si practicas estar preocupada por cada pequeño detalle en tu relación, esto se puede convertir en una obsesión que potencialmente dañara tu relación.  Si en cambio te enfocas en abrir las líneas de comunicación, le dejas saber lo que esperas de él y discuten cómo pueden trabajar juntos para recuperar la confianza, pueden volverse más cercanos y darse la oportunidad de que la relación crezca.

My spirituality plays a significant role in my life, but lately, I've been feeling disconnected from it. I'm struggling to find meaning and purpose, and it's affecting my overall well-being. I hope to delve deeper into my spiritual beliefs and understand how they can contribute to my emotional and mental health.

Finding meaning and purpose in our lives is a deeply personal journey, and I understand that feeling disconnected from your spirituality can be challenging. It's great that you are recognizing the importance of exploring your spiritual beliefs and how they can contribute to your emotional and mental well-being. Here are some suggestions that may help you delve deeper into your spirituality:

1. Take time for self-reflection: Set aside dedicated time each day or week to reflect on your spiritual beliefs. Journaling can be a helpful way to explore your thoughts, feelings, and experiences related to spirituality.

2. Engage in mindful practices: Mindfulness exercises such as meditation, deep breathing, or grounding techniques can create space for you to connect with your spirituality. Focus on being present in the moment and observe any thoughts or emotions that arise.

3. Seek out community: Consider finding a supportive community of like-minded individuals who share similar spiritual beliefs. This could be through joining a local religious or spiritual group, attending retreats, or participating in online forums.

4. Explore different spiritual resources: Read books, listen to podcasts, or watch videos that align with your spiritual interests. These resources can provide new perspectives and insights, allowing you to deepen your understanding and connection to your spirituality.

5. Connect with nature: Spending time outdoors and appreciating the beauty of nature can be a powerful way to reconnect with your spirituality. Take walks in nature, visit parks, or simply sit outside and observe the world around you.

6. Practice gratitude: Cultivating an attitude of gratitude can enhance your spiritual connection and overall well-being. Take time each day to acknowledge and appreciate the blessings and positive aspects of your life.

7. Be patient and compassionate with yourself: Remember that exploring spirituality is a personal journey, and it takes time. Allow yourself to go at your own pace and be gentle with yourself if you encounter challenges along the way. 

By incorporating these suggestions into your routine, you may find that you are able to reconnect with your spirituality and discover how it can positively impact your emotional and mental health. Remember, this is a process of self-discovery, so embrace the journey and be open to learning and growth.

Multiple factors contribute to my current stress level, including work demands, financial worries, and personal relationship conflicts.

A recent example that triggered my stress was an unexpected car breakdown, which resulted in additional expenses. This sudden financial strain worsened my overall stress levels as I worried about meeting my financial obligations and managing unexpected emergencies. Since then, I have been constantly feeling on edge, experiencing irritability, and having trouble sleeping. These symptoms occur frequently throughout the day.

In terms of family dynamics, there is often a high level of tension and conflict, which adds to my stress levels. Additionally, significant life events such as moving to a new city, adjusting to a demanding job, and taking care of multiple responsibilities contribute to this ongoing stress.

To cope with stress, I have tried engaging in regular exercise and practicing relaxation techniques. Although they provide temporary relief, the stress always seems to return. I am curious about other strategies or therapeutic approaches that might help me effectively manage stress and prevent it from negatively impacting my well-being.

It's evident that stress has been playing a significant role in your life lately, and it's commendable that you're seeking ways to manage it in order to safeguard your physical and mental well-being. By identifying various factors contributing to your stress level, such as work demands, financial worries, and personal relationship conflicts, you've already taken an important step towards addressing the issue.

The unexpected car breakdown that caused additional expenses certainly added to your stress. Financial strain can be particularly overwhelming, leading to constant worry about meeting obligations and handling unforeseen emergencies. It's understandable that this has left you feeling on edge, experiencing irritability, and struggling with sleep disturbances throughout the day.

Your family dynamics also contribute to your stress levels, as tension and conflict exist within those relationships. Additionally, major life events like moving to a new city, adjusting to a demanding job, and managing multiple responsibilities further intensify your ongoing stress.

In terms of coping mechanisms, engaging in regular exercise and practicing relaxation techniques are excellent strategies for managing stress. They provide a temporary sense of relief, which is beneficial. However, it's disheartening to hear that your stress consistently returns. 

To help effectively manage stress and prevent it from negatively impacting your overall well-being, I would suggest exploring other approaches and therapeutic options. One valuable tool is cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), which focuses on identifying and modifying unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors. CBT can teach you skills to challenge negative thoughts related to stressors and develop healthier coping mechanisms.

Another approach worth considering is mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR). MBSR involves practicing mindfulness techniques, such as meditation and deep breathing exercises, to cultivate present-moment awareness and reduce stress reactivity. This can aid in developing a calmer mindset and increased resilience when facing stressors.

You may also benefit from exploring stress management workshops or support groups in your community. These resources often provide practical techniques, a sense of community support, and the opportunity to learn from others who are navigating similar challenges.

Remember that stress management is a process, and what works for one person may not work for another. It's essential to find strategies that resonate with you personally. Experimenting with various approaches can help you discover what brings you lasting relief. If you're open to it, maintaining an open line of communication with your loved ones about how certain dynamics affect your stress levels might also foster understanding and create room for potential resolutions.

Overall, please know that there are multiple paths to effectively managing stress, and it's encouraging to see your commitment in seeking out healthier coping mechanisms. Exploring therapeutic approaches like CBT or MBSR, engaging in stress management workshops or support groups, as well as continuing to take care of yourself through exercise and relaxation techniques will enable you to develop a sustainable approach to stress management and protect your overall well-being.

My relationships with my family members have become strained recently, especially with my parents. It's affecting my mental health, as I constantly feel misunderstood and disconnected from them. Through counseling, I would like to explore how to improve communication and rebuild these important relationships.

Building and maintaining healthy relationships can be challenging, especially within the dynamics of a family. It's great that you're seeking guidance to improve communication and reconnect with your parents. Here are some suggestions:

1. Self-reflection: Take some time to reflect on your own feelings, needs, and expectations in these relationships. Understanding yourself better will allow you to express your thoughts and emotions more effectively.

2. Active Listening: Approach conversations with an open mind and actively listen to what your family members have to say. Avoid interrupting or assuming their intentions. Validating their perspectives can help create a safe space for open communication.

3. Empathy and Understanding: Try to put yourself in your parents' shoes and see situations from their perspective. This can help foster empathy and understand their motivations or concerns. Remember, acknowledging their viewpoints doesn't mean you have to agree with them.

4. Express Your Feelings: Find appropriate moments to express your thoughts, feelings, and needs to your parents. Be clear, honest, and assertive without being confrontational or blaming. Using "I statements" (e.g., "I feel...") often helps convey your emotions effectively.

5. Seek Common Ground: Discover shared interests or activities that can serve as a common ground for building connection and bonding with your parents. Engaging in positive experiences together can strengthen your relationship and create opportunities for meaningful conversations.

6. Practice Forgiveness: Holding onto past grudges or resentments can hinder progress in rebuilding relationships. Consider forgiveness as a means of letting go of negative emotions and fostering healing. It's not about forgetting the past but rather moving forward with a fresh perspective.

7. Patience and Flexibility: Rebuilding relationships takes time; it won't happen overnight. Be patient with both yourself and your family members as you navigate through this journey. Acknowledge that change may be gradual and be flexible in adapting to new ways of interacting.

8. Seek Support: Consider reaching out to friends, support groups, or online communities where you can engage with others who may be going through similar experiences. Sharing your thoughts and receiving support from others can offer additional perspectives and coping strategies.

Remember, healing relationships is a collaborative effort. However, it's essential to take care of yourself throughout this process. Engaging in self-care activities, such as exercise, hobbies, or journaling, can help manage stress and contribute to your overall well-being.

You are right. It is not normal to hear voices that aren't your own but the fact is some people do. In my experience, medication seem to help. It is also important to understand when you hear voices the most - meaning it is important to understand what the triggers are. It is also important to understand when the voices are the least - meaning what helps you deal with the voices better. My clients have reported that their triggers are being in social gathering or around strangers or for some even the TV. Trying to identify your triggers is helpful for some people. Clients have also reported that listening to music, watching TV, being with friend or family helps them deal with their voices. Every individual is different and you need to figure out what works for you and what triggers your voices. I've noticed a pattern where I experience deep sadness, lack of motivation, and a general feeling of emptiness for prolonged periods. It significantly affects my ability to function on a day-to-day basis. My objective is to get to the root cause of these depressive episodes and develop tools to better cope with them.

It's difficult to experience deep sadness, lack of motivation, and a general feeling of emptiness for prolonged periods. I can hear that it significantly affects your ability to function on a day-to-day basis. Your objective of getting to the root cause of these depressive episodes and developing tools to better cope with them is a great step towards improving your well-being. Here are some suggestions and guidance:

1. Self-reflection: Take some time to reflect on any possible triggers or patterns that may be contributing to your depressive episodes. Are there certain situations, events, or thoughts that seem to precede these episodes? Journaling your feelings and experiences can help you gain insights.

2. Support system: Reach out to trusted friends or family members who can provide emotional support during challenging times. Remember, you don't have to go through this alone. Sometimes, talking about your feelings with someone who cares and understands can make a significant difference.

3. Healthy lifestyle: Engage in activities that promote physical and mental well-being. Regular exercise, proper nutrition, and sufficient sleep can positively impact your overall mood. Additionally, consider incorporating relaxation techniques such as mindfulness or meditation into your routine.

4. Cognitive reframing: Notice any negative thought patterns or self-talk that might be perpetuating your depressive episodes. Practice challenging those thoughts and replacing them with more realistic and positive ones. It takes time and effort, but this shift in mindset can lead to improved coping mechanisms.

5. Professional help: If your symptoms persist or worsen despite your efforts, seeking professional help from a mental health expert could be beneficial. They can provide you with personalized guidance, therapy options like cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), or even medication if necessary. However, remember that taking this step is ultimately up to you and should be done at your own pace.

6. Hobbies and interests: Engage in activities that bring you joy and fulfillment. Pursue hobbies or interests that you enjoy, as these can provide a sense of purpose and distraction from negative thoughts.

7. Gratitude practice: Cultivate gratitude by focusing on the positive aspects of your life. Take some time each day to reflect on things you are thankful for, no matter how small. This practice can help shift your focus towards optimism and improve your overall mood.

Remember, everyone's journey is unique, so find what works best for you. It may take some trial and error to discover which coping strategies and support systems resonate most with you. Be patient with yourself and know that progress takes time.

How do you know you have the right therapist for you?
 How would I know how to "train" my therapist to be able to give me what I need from treatment?

What an important question! I think one of the first things to assess is this: Do you feel comfortable with your therapist? Do you feel like you can talk openly about what's going on in your life without feeling judged? Do you experience your therapy as a safe space to process your thoughts and feelings? Feeling comfortable with your therapist is a crucial factor. Once you feel comfortable with your therapist, you can have a conversation about what works for you in therapy. Tell your therapist what is helpful, and what you don't find helpful. A skilled therapist can shift his or her style and techniques to meet your individual needs, and this may be an ongoing conversation that the two of you have during therapy. Oftentimes, there is just an X factor between client and therapist that either makes the relationship work or can make it feel like something is missing. This is no one's fault, it's just that not every therapist will be a perfect match for every client. If you feel uncomfortable with your therapist or feel like that x factor is missing, it is a good idea to keep searching for therapist who is right for you.

One approach that may be helpful is psychotherapy, which focuses on understanding the underlying causes of your depression and developing strategies to address them. This might involve exploring past experiences and relationships, identifying negative thought patterns and beliefs, and developing coping mechanisms to manage stress and emotions.

Additionally, consider engaging in activities that bring you joy and help you connect with others, such as pursuing a hobby or joining a support group. These activities can provide a sense of purpose and help you build resilience.

It's also essential to practice self-compassion and self-care during this time. Remember that healing from depression takes time, and it's important to be patient and compassionate with yourself throughout the process.

It's important to remember that every person's journey with mental health is unique, and there is no one-size-fits-all solution. I encourage you to continue exploring different treatment options and working closely with your healthcare provider to find the best approach for you.

Hello, I'm in need of guidance regarding my relationships. My goal is to gain insight into forming healthier connections and addressing patterns of toxic dynamics in my friendships. Lately, I've noticed that I often attract manipulative individuals who take advantage of my kindness and empathy. One specific situation that exemplifies this issue was when I loaned a significant amount of money to a friend in need, only to discover later that they had used it irresponsibly and avoided repayment. This left me feeling betrayed and questioning whether I can trust anyone anymore. How can I establish boundaries, identify red flags, and cultivate healthy relationships moving forward?

Building healthier connections and addressing toxic dynamics in friendships is a commendable goal. It's unfortunate that you have been attracting manipulative individuals who take advantage of your kindness and empathy. The specific situation you mentioned, where you loaned money to a friend and they misused it without repaying, must have been incredibly painful and left you questioning trust.

To establish boundaries and cultivate healthier relationships moving forward, here are some suggestions:

1. Reflect on Your Relationships: Take some time for introspection and self-reflection. Consider the patterns within your past relationships and any commonalities among the manipulative individuals you've encountered. This can help you identify red flags and be more aware of potential warning signs in future friendships.

2. Recognize Your Needs and Values: Clarify what you value most in a friendship - trust, respect, reciprocity, or support. Knowing your needs and values will enable you to better understand when these are being compromised or violated. Prioritizing your own well-being while setting healthy boundaries is crucial.

3. Set Clear Boundaries: Be assertive and communicate your boundaries effectively from the beginning of friendships. Let others know what behaviors are acceptable and unacceptable to you. It may feel uncomfortable at first, but establishing clear boundaries early on helps create healthier dynamics.

4. Trust Your Gut Feelings: Pay attention to your instincts and intuition. Often, our intuition alerts us to potential problems before we consciously recognize them. If something doesn't feel right, take the time to step back and evaluate the situation before proceeding further.

5. Practice Self-Care: Nurturing yourself emotionally, physically, and mentally is key to maintaining healthy relationships. Engage in activities that bring you joy, reduce stress, and promote your overall well-being. When you prioritize self-care, you become better equipped to navigate challenges and make informed choices about whom you allow into your life.

6. Seek Balanced Reciprocity: Healthy relationships are built on mutual respect and support. Look for friendships where there is a balance of give and take, rather than one-sided dynamics. Cultivate connections with individuals who demonstrate genuine care and reciprocate kindness.

7. Utilize Supportive Networks: Surround yourself with supportive people who uplift you and encourage personal growth. Connecting with positive social networks such as hobby groups, community organizations, or interest-based clubs can lead to meeting like-minded individuals who share common values.

Remember, developing healthier relationships takes time and effort. Give yourself permission to learn from past experiences, grow, and gradually build stronger connections that align with your aspirations and values.

Thanks for reaching out and asking this question.  Social stuff is hard.  Even for people that don't have diagnosed social anxiety.  Some research outlines that our fear of public speaking is greater than our fear of death.  That's hefty!  Shame is often the culprit for social anxiety because we think other people will see the flaws in ourselves that we believe are there.  I've had experiences where I thought the person thought something awful of me, just to find out it was exactly the opposite.  That's how powerful our minds can be!What are other things that people may think of you?  Maybe you are very kind and easy to talk to.  Maybe you think differently than other people and some people enjoy hearing your perspectives.  It's even a possibility that they are worrying about the same things as you, even if they seem very confident.  Confidence can be easy to fake if it's how you cope with fear.To work through some of that, it's much better to force yourself out there and have conversations.  Avoiding people sends the message to your brain that not only are those situations dangerous (socially), but that you can't handle them.  The more you avoid, the harder it gets and the more anxiety is created by just the thought of being around people.  Take it moment by moment, too.  Thinking about all the conversations you are confronted with in a day is overwhelming.  Just focus Why is Citizen Kane considered the Best Film?

The American Film Institute and the British Film Institute have Citizen Kane listed as the number one movie of all time.  The British Film Institute has had this rating of Citizen Kane for 50 years.  There are multitudes of reasons why this is a deserving title with a few examples below.

1. Citizen Kane was a thinly veiled movie about a powerful person.  Even before the movie was released newspaper magnate William R Hearst became aware that Kane had many similarities to Hearst.  Both controlled media empires, ran for office, and had giant mansions filled with odds and ends.  Where it allegedly became personal was when scenes showing Kane's wife put through an humiliating run in showbiz propped up by Kane's largesse mirrored Hearst a bit too closely to real life.  Hearst reportedly offered to buy all copies of the film and told newspapers to not print anything or even mention its name.

The stress from work has started affecting my sleep patterns. I often find myself lying awake at night, unable to switch off my racing thoughts. It takes me hours to fall asleep, and even then, I wake up multiple times throughout the night. As a result, I feel tired and fatigued during the day, which further adds to my stress levels.

It sounds like you're experiencing a lot of stress from work, which is impacting your sleep patterns. When we have racing thoughts that keep us awake at night, it can be really frustrating and exhausting. Here are some suggestions that might help improve your sleep:

1. Establish a bedtime routine: Creating a consistent routine before bed can signal to your body that it's time to wind down. This could include activities such as reading a book, taking a warm bath, or practicing relaxation techniques like deep breathing or meditation.

2. Create a sleep-friendly environment: Make sure your bedroom is a comfortable and relaxing space. Keep the room cool, dark, and quiet. Consider using earplugs or a white noise machine if external noises are disruptive. Also, try to limit screen time before bed as the blue light emitted by electronic devices can interfere with sleep.

3. Manage your racing thoughts: If your mind tends to race with thoughts and worries when you lie down to sleep, it can be helpful to practice mindfulness or cognitive techniques. One technique is to write down your thoughts in a journal before bed, allowing yourself to release them from your mind. You can also try progressive muscle relaxation or guided imagery exercises to help calm your mind.

4. Stick to a regular sleep schedule: Try to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends. This helps regulate your body's internal clock and promotes better sleep quality over time.

5. Limit caffeine and alcohol intake: Both caffeine and alcohol can disrupt sleep patterns. It's best to avoid consuming these substances close to bedtime, especially if you're already struggling with sleep issues.

6. Engage in physical activity: Regular exercise during the day can help reduce stress levels and promote better sleep. However, try to finish exercising at least a few hours before bedtime, as exercising too close to bedtime may actually make it harder for you to fall asleep.

Remember, improving sleep patterns takes time and patience. If these suggestions don't seem to make a significant difference, it may be helpful to consult with a healthcare professional who can provide further guidance tailored to your specific situation.

Hello, my anxiety has started interfering with my sleep patterns. Every night, when I try to fall asleep, my mind races with irrational thoughts and worries. The fear of not being able to wake up on time or complete my tasks the next day is constantly on my mind. This heightened state of alertness keeps me awake for hours, leading to exhaustion and irritability the following day.
Through counseling, I seek techniques to manage my anxiety before bedtime. I want to establish healthy sleep habits and reclaim restful nights that will allow me to face each day with energy and focus.

One technique that may help manage your anxiety before bedtime is practicing relaxation exercises. Deep breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, and guided imagery are all methods that can help calm your mind and body. Try incorporating these techniques into a bedtime routine to signal to your brain that it's time to unwind.

Creating a relaxing sleep environment can also be beneficial. Keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet. Remove any distractions, such as electronic devices or work-related materials, from the bedroom. Consider using white noise machines or soothing music to drown out external noises.

Establishing a consistent sleep schedule can contribute to better sleep quality as well. Try going to bed and waking up at the same time each day, even on weekends. This helps regulate your body's internal clock and optimize the natural sleep-wake cycle.

Before bed, it can be helpful to engage in calming activities that promote relaxation and reduce anxiety. Reading a book, taking a warm bath, or practicing gentle stretching or yoga can all help you unwind and prepare for sleep.

It's important to avoid stimulating substances like caffeine, nicotine, and alcohol close to bedtime, as they can disrupt your sleep. Instead, opt for herbal teas or warm milk if you find that a nighttime drink is comforting.

If racing thoughts continue to keep you awake, consider keeping a journal or writing down your worries before bed. This can help offload anxious thoughts from your mind, allowing you to relax more easily.

Lastly, establishing healthy boundaries around technology use can greatly benefit your sleep. Avoid using screens, such as smartphones or tablets, for at least an hour before bed. The blue light emitted by these devices can interfere with your body's melatonin production, making it harder to fall asleep.

Remember, practicing these techniques consistently over time can lead to improved sleep patterns. However, if your symptoms persist or worsen, it might be helpful to consult a mental health professional who can provide tailored guidance and support.

It sounds like you've been experiencing a lot of distress and a loss of enjoyment in activities that used to bring you joy. The constant cloud hanging over you can be really overwhelming, and it's understandable that you're feeling scared by these changes. Difficulty sleeping and struggling to find motivation are also common symptoms when going through a tough time.

To begin addressing this heavy feeling of sadness and regaining your motivation, it may be helpful to start with small steps. First, consider reaching out to someone trustworthy in your support network, such as a friend or family member. Sharing what you're going through can provide relief and potentially open the door for additional support.

In addition, engaging in activities that you used to enjoy, even if they might not bring you immediate pleasure, can still be beneficial. You mentioned painting and spending time with friends - try setting aside some time each week to engage in those activities again, even if it feels challenging at first. Gradually reintroducing them into your routine could reignite your passion and connect you with positive experiences.

Taking care of your physical health is equally important. Make sure you're getting regular exercise, eating balanced meals, and trying to stick to a consistent sleep schedule. Creating healthy habits can have a positive impact on your overall well-being.

Exploring new coping strategies can also help alleviate your symptoms. Look into relaxation techniques such as deep breathing exercises, meditation, or guided imagery. These practices can be done anywhere and can assist in reducing stress and promoting restful sleep.

Remember, navigating through difficult emotions takes time and patience. It would also be beneficial to consult a mental health professional who can offer guidance tailored specifically to your needs. They can explore potential underlying causes, provide coping strategies specific to your situation, and create an effective treatment plan.

Please keep in mind that my suggestions are not meant to replace the advice of a mental health expert, so I encourage you to reach out to a professional who can assist you further on your journey toward healing.

We've been in a long distance relationship for two and a half years. I recently saw his phone and saw the people he texts the most and one of them was a female coworker. I don't know how to approach this situation. How do I ask him about it?.

Just ask him.I'm not sure how you saw his phone if you're in a long distance relationship, because long distance means you live far apart from each other and don't get to see each other in person. Therefore, I think we may have a different understanding of the definition of "long distance relationship" which makes it hard for me to adequately answer this question for you.I don't know how old you are, but if you're an adult, after two and a half years, I don't think it's unreasonable to have an open and honest talk with each other about where the relationship is going and what you both want and expect. Long distance relationships are difficult to keep alive because you don't ever see each other in person. Talking, texting, and video chatting isn't enough, and the longer the physical distance remains, the more difficult it becomes to keep an emotional closeness. It may be time to evaluate the situation, figure out when (if ever) the two of you will be able to be together in person, and if you can and want to wait that long. Do you both want the same things out of life? If one of you wants to take the relationship to the next level but the other doesn't, then it doesn't matter if it's long distance or not - if you aren't on the same page with the relationship, it is going to be difficult to make it work.Trust is important. Issues with trust, insecurity, jealousy, lying and/or hiding things from each other, being afraid to speak up and have an honest conversation - these things can ruin relationships if not addressed. I know confrontation of any sort can be hard for some people, but it is necessary at times. Evaluate your true feelings for him. Are you with him for reasons other than love, such as being afraid to be alone or thinking you wouldn't be able to find someone else? Has he ever given you reason to be suspicious of his female coworkers or friends before? Some people, unfortunately, develop a track record of indiscretions and give their significant others ample reason for distrusting them. However, if this is not the case, you may be unfairly judging his texting through the eyes of your own insecurities. It may be time for you both to take an honest assessment of your own reasons for being in the relationship, figure out what you want, and make a decision. This may result in bringing the two of you closer and taking the relationship to the next level. Or, it could lead to a decision to end things. I know that can be difficult, but you both deserve to be happy and to be allowed to make the decisions that will lead to your personal happiness.

The best way to move on is to give yourself sufficient time and space away from your ex so you can heal.  That means no checking out your ex on social media platforms and no contact.  In order to move on and diminish the obsessions, help yourself recognize and accept that the relationship is over, and make sure to get sufficient support in processing all your feelings.  Once that takes place, it can be useful to explore and process with a professional the meaning of the relationship and to understand your part in what transpired.Sometimes people obsess because they have difficulties accepting what's already taken place and want things to be different.  The key to moving forward is to be loving toward yourself, to give yourself permission to grieve the loss, and to start cultivating new and healthy habits/patterns.  Reengage in your present life, ask yourself what you want your life to look like, and start creating goals and taking small steps to create the amazing life you want for yourself.

Try not to blame yourself for the situation and focus on taking practical steps towards improving your circumstances. Small, consistent efforts over time can lead to positive changes.

Lately, I've been under a tremendous amount of stress at work. The workload keeps piling up, deadlines are approaching rapidly, and I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities. This stress has started to spill over into other areas of my life, making it difficult for me to relax and enjoy my free time. I often find myself unable to sleep properly due to racing thoughts about work-related issues. Through counseling, I hope to find ways to better handle stress and create a healthier work-life balance.

It sounds like you've been dealing with a lot of stress at work lately. The increasing workload and approaching deadlines can definitely make it feel overwhelming, and I understand how that can spill over into other areas of your life. It's great that you're seeking counseling to find ways to handle stress and create a healthier work-life balance. Here are some suggestions that might help:

1. Prioritize and delegate: Take a step back and assess your workload. Identify the most important tasks and focus on those first. If possible, delegate some responsibilities to lighten your load.

2. Set boundaries: Establish clear boundaries between work and personal life. Avoid checking emails or doing work-related tasks during your free time. Give yourself permission to disconnect and engage in activities that bring you joy and relaxation.

3. Time management: Develop effective time management strategies to better organize your tasks. Break down larger projects into smaller, manageable steps. Use tools like calendars or to-do lists to prioritize and track your progress.

4. Self-care: Make self-care a priority. Engage in activities that promote relaxation and well-being, such as exercise, meditation, or hobbies you enjoy. Taking care of your physical and mental health will improve your ability to handle stress.

5. Seek support: Don't hesitate to reach out for support from friends, family, or colleagues. Talking about your concerns and sharing your feelings can provide valuable perspective and emotional support.

6. Communication: Openly communicate with your supervisor or colleagues about your workload and any challenges you may be facing. They may be able to offer assistance or suggest strategies to manage your tasks more effectively.

7. Boundaries with technology: Limit your exposure to work-related technology outside of working hours. Consider setting specific times when you turn off notifications or even temporarily uninstalling work-related apps from your phone.

8. Relaxation techniques: Explore different relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, or guided imagery. These techniques can help calm your mind and promote better sleep.

Remember, finding a healthier work-life balance takes time and experimentation. Be patient with yourself as you explore different strategies and make adjustments along the way. Your counselor will be able to provide additional guidance and support throughout this process.

My mother-in-law is mentally ill. She has been for most of her life. She cuts herself. She has been in and out of psychiatric hospitals for about 40 years. She has voices in her head that tell her to cut herself. She has had multiple shock therapy treatments, and she’s on enough medication to take down an elephant. Her parental rights for her two children were taken away from her when my husband was a boy—he is now in his late 30s. She doesn’t even have custody of herself. She hasn’t asked yet, but she has been insinuating that she wants to babysit my child. How do I go about saying no without creating an issue?

Hi Fontana,Thanks for providing all the details needed in order to respond to your question. It seems very clear to me that "no" would be the appropriate response. I like your healthy boundaries, and I'll help you explore possible ways to respond to her. First, she hasn't asked yet, and you don't know that she will. Right now, you can pleasantly ignore her hints. They're not hurting you and if you ignore them, they're more likely to go away. You can address and reduce your own anxiety about the possibility of her asking by reassuring yourself that you have the right as parents to make this decision, and that if she's offended, that doesn't mean that you're being mean; it means that she has unrealistic expectations. So, the first goal is to put it out of your mind as a worry. You might never have to face that moment. But, I understand that you want to be prepared.As her son, perhaps your husband is the best one to answer the question, should it ever come. Is he willing to do this? But if you are comfortable, and if you're the one she asks, you can confidently give her a simple, honest response about why it won't happen. And I would suggest presenting a firmly closed door, rather than saying "but maybe later". No need to apologize or hum and haw..."We love that you want to be around Junior, and we definitely want you in his/her life. (try to leave out the "but" here). You're not in a healthy place, and we're not comfortable with you caring for him/her on your own."If she pushes the issue, this is evidence of her denial or inappropriate boundaries. I'd let her know that it's not negotiable, that you understand if she's disappointed, but you're not open to discussing the issue. Really, there's nothing to discuss. Learning not to take responsibility for her emotions is part of having an ill person in your life. I wish you the best.

We had our first kid 15 years ago, and sex has been nonexistent ever since. It only happens every three or four months. We have been to counseling, and I have been told over and over again she will come around. She hasn't, and I'm intimately lonely! I think it's time to move on, but how do I do that without hurting my kids?

Hi Pocahontas, This is a painful situation. When you're in a relationship, you assume that you will continue to receive warmth and affection. When it dries up, it's a very lonely place. It's possible that there is an unaddressed issue in the relationship. It's also possible that your partner has hormonal issues, pain issues,  sexual dysfunction or is asexual. There is no one answer here. Only you can decide what is right for you. But let me ask some questions to help you explore next steps:Aside from the sex, is your wife loving and supportive? What are the other ways in which you feel loved? Does your wife talk to you? Does she communicate her needs and desires? Does she articulate what gets in the way of having sex? If your wife is generally a loving, open partner, you use this to see that her behaviours aren't personal. Whether she resolves this or not, it can help you to cope with the rejection. This is your wife's issue, and the "ball" is in her court.In my opinion, if couple's therapy hasn't helped, it's time for your wife to own whatever is blocking her and address it with her physician and therapist. Let her be in charge of the sex for a while, to take the pressure off, and she can have the time to figure out what gets in the way of having regular sexual intimacy in your relationship. If you think of this as "my wife is in crisis and needs support in figuring this out", it can help you manage your own emotions. Pressure to have sex might push her further away. Did the couple therapist help you to see the dynamic in your relationship? Has your partner identified something she feels she is lacking in the relationship? One good way to make sure you "get" is to "give" (and I mean give what she wants, not sex). It's appropriate to say to her now "I cannot live in a relationship with so little intimacy. I need for you to be honest with me about what you want for us sexually. If this is all you want, I'm not sure I can do it. If you want us to be more sexual, I need you to address what gets in the way for you."  Give her some time, help her in any way you can, and then see where you are. See if she does seek help to address an issue that is hers. Then...you have a decision to make. I encourage you to make it looking at the big picture, not just the sex.
